movesets.name: Flame Orb
movesets.description:
Trailblaze lets Heracross get around ordinary revenge killers such as Rotom-Heat and Choice Scarf Florges. Swords Dance is better if Heracross wishes to focus purely on wallbreaking, allowing it to push past physically bulky foes like Palossand. Megahorn slams walls like Vileplume and Amoonguss without requiring Heracross to Terastallize or set up.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Spikes can be used to capitalize on the switches Heracross forces, though Megahorn offers strong coverage against the likes of Galarian Slowbro and Venusaur, which can otherwise blank Heracross.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

strategies.overview: Heracross offers itself to teams as a strong wallbreaker that can break holes into foes. Its access to Guts allows Heracross to switch in against status attempts from foes like Vaporeon and Amoonguss while giving it an extra power boost. Heracross's above average bulk lets it handle wallbreakers such as Scrafty, Breloom, and Overqwil. Furthermore, Heracross can punish teams that rely on common defensive Pokemon like Bellibolt, Wo-Chien, and Vaporeon. However, it lacks any longevity, making repeatedly switching in difficult for Heracross due to entry hazards and burn damage. Furthermore, Heracross's mediocre Speed tier makes it easily revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Barraskewda, Flamigo, and Choice Scarf Chandelure.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Throat Chop allows Heracross to better handle sound users like Sylveon and Toxtricity, but it prefers to run Knock Off to better handle item-reliant foes like Avalugg and Gligar. Heracross can run a Choice Scarf set with Moxie to outpace faster threats like Kilowattrel and Chandelure, but it's completely outclassed by other Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo due to them having a higher Speed stat. Spikes can also be used, making Heracross a solid entry hazard setter with the ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from walls like Amoonguss and Avalugg. However, Spikes is very niche, and Heracross prefers to run the Guts set.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Offensive Flying-types like Flamigo, Tornadus, and Kilowattrel can destroy Heracross with their attacks, but none of them enjoy switching into its Guts-boosted Facade. Defensive Flying-types like Gligar and Altaria can tank its Close Combat; the former can freely set up entry hazards, while the latter can destroy Heracross with Brave Bird. However, neither of them enjoy switching into Knock Off and Facade.

Fire-types: Choice Scarf Chandelure, Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-F can outspeed Heracross and destroy it with their STAB attacks, but they have to be cautious of switching into its powerful attacks.

Psychic-types: Faster Psychic-types like Munkidori, Scream Tail and Meloetta can easily revenge kill Heracross, but none of them enjoy switching directly into Knock Off and Facade. Bulky walls like Galarian Slowbro and Uxie can tank its Close Combat while threatening Heracross back with their attacks or free setup.

movesets.name: Guts Wallbreaker
movesets.description:
Set Details

Knock Off is good coverage against Ghost-types like Chandelure and Decidueye as well as Psychic-types like Galarian Slowbro and Uxie that also threatens Pokemon heavily reliant on their held items like Incineroar, Kilowattrel, and Porygon2. Facade synergizes well with Guts, allowing Heracross to put major damage on foes that resist its Close Combat like Toxicroak, Amoonguss, and Sylveon. Trailblaze lets it outpace foes like Kilowattrel and Infernape after one use, whereas Megahorn can hit Grass- and Psychic-types like Tsareena and Meloetta. Alternatively, Heracross can opt to run Swords Dance, which makes it a terrifying setup sweeper. Tera Dark boosts the power of Knock Off while giving Heracross a useful Psychic-type immunity against foes like Munkidori and Galarian Articuno. Tera Normal gives Facade an extra power boost, allowing it to 2HKO defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss, while giving Heracross a useful immunity to Ghost-type attacks from Chandelure and Decidueye.

Heracross partners well with Fire-resistant Pokemon like Incineroar, Vaporeon, and Basculegion-M, as they handle Fire-types such as Chandelure and Paldean Tauros-F. Pivots like Flygon, Munkidori, and Inteleon can bring in threats Heracross can easily take advantage of like Amoonguss, Copperajah, and Vaporeon while also helping Heracross activate its Flame Orb safely. Additionally, slow pivots like Swampert, Bellibolt, and Incineroar can help Heracross enter the field and activate its Flame Orb safely. Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Duraludon are great partners, since they can handle Flying- and Psychic-types like Tornadus and Munkidori. Heracross synergizes with other wallbreakers like Flygon, Barraskewda, and Munkidori to overwhelm defensive tanks like Amoonguss, Bronzong, and Rhyperior. Entry hazard removers like Avalugg, Tsareena, and Altaria help it avoid getting pressured when switching into hazards.

strategies.overview:
Bug

Heracross finds a niche as a physical wallbreaker, leveraging its Fighting typing and Guts to alleviate Rock and Steel matchups while also dismantling Poison team cores with its combination of Swords Dance + Guts-boosted Facade; however, due to that same typing and its below average Speed, it struggles against common Fairy- and Psychic-types like Iron Valiant and Latios and is a less-than-ideal choice. Furthermore, Heracross faces direct competition for its role from Life Orb Slither Wing, which also has U-turn and has access to reliable recovery. Heracross is also outclassed by other physical attackers like Scizor and Lokix, both possessing crucial priority options, with Scizor also being more adept at handling Rock and Fairy teams. Lastly, Volcarona, with its Fire typing and access to Quiver Dance, serves as a powerful special wallbreaker, outclassing Heracross as an answer to Steel-types barring Heatran.

movesets.name: Guts Attacker (Bug)
movesets.description:
Heracross is a niche wallbreaker for Bug teams by virtue of its high Attack, Fighting typing, Swords Dance, and the ability Guts, capable of easing Rock, Steel, and Poison matchups. Close Combat eliminates Rock- and Steel-types like Tyranitar and Heatran and, when at +2, allows Heracross to break through walls like Skarmory, Mandibuzz, and Great Tusk. Facade complements Close Combat by targeting Flying-, Fairy-, and Poison-types, outright OHKOing Gliscor and Primarina at +2 and OHKOing Galarian Weezing and Toxapex at +2 after minimal chip damage. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo and Slowbro, and it removes Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from the aforementioned walls, wearing them down, which is especially helpful if Heracross opts to use Trailblaze as its fourth move. Trailblaze allows Heracross to outspeed faster foes like Ogerpon formes, Latios, and Choice Scarf Heatran, making it an excellent late-game cleaner. However, without Swords Dance, Heracross struggles to break walls like Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, and Iron Defense Skarmory.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is an essential teammate, serving as a revenge killer and utilizing its Rock typing to eliminate pesky Fire- and Flying-types like Ogerpon-H, Ninetales, Tornadus-T, and Dragonite, which pose a serious threat to Bug teams, while simultaneously setting Stealth Rock with Stone Axe. Araquanid provides Sticky Web support, which allows Heracross to outspeed would-be faster foes like the Ogerpon formes, Dragapult, and, when at +1, even Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada and Greninja. Araquanid can also take advantage of its superb special bulk and Fire resistance provided by Water Bubble to take on Fire-types like Volcarona and Iron Moth. Additionally, Araquanid can use Mirror Coat to get a surprise OHKO on foes like Choice Specs Latios and Flutter Mane. Scizor and Lokix cover Heracross's weaknesses; Scizor eliminates Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant, while Lokix threatens Psychic- and Ghost-types like Latios and Dragapult; both teammates also deal with faster Rock-types like Iron Boulder and Ogerpon-C, which Heracross might struggle against. In return, Heracross can handle physical walls like Archaludon, Toxapex, and Mandibuzz. Forretress sets entry hazards, provides safe entry to Heracross with its slow Volt Switch, and removes hazards with Rapid Spin. Heracross's ability to break through special walls like Alolan Muk, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra is greatly appreciated by teammates like Volcarona and Frosmoth. In return, Volcarona can spread burns to weaken physical attackers like Dragonite and Zamazenta, and Frosmoth can eliminate Flying-, Ground-, Dragon-types like Zapdos, Hippowdon, and Dragonite.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Heracross is a very strong physical attacker with great abilities that allow it to wallbreak or even win games, but it often finds itself outclassed by other options. Its Speed tier is workable with a Choice Scarf or Trailblaze boost, but it is mediocre at best otherwise. It does provide important resistances to Ground, Dark, and Fighting along with Spikes support, but its bulk isn't notable enough to take hits reliably, and its typing and stats aren't ideal to make full use of its utility. Its offensive coverage is excellent, but its STAB combination isn't great. Heracross is all about having a lot of great qualities, but each of those qualities has a significant drawback, keeping it as a viable but niche option in Draft.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Heracross leverages its high Attack, strong STAB moves, and further damage modifiers from Guts or a damage-boosting item to easily break through foes' defenses. These sets can occasionally run Swords Dance to further boost its wallbreaking power or Trailblaze to enable Heracross as a potential late-game wincon that can outspeed foes as well.

Revenge Killer: Heracross's decent Speed stat with a Choice Scarf and Moxie allows it to revenge kill foes and act as a cleaner late-game, since it can snowball with Attack boosts.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Megahorn, Lunge, Close Combat, Low Kick

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Bulk Up, Trailblaze

Utility Moves: Brick Break, Spikes, Substitute

Coverage: Double-Edge, Earthquake, Facade, High Horsepower, Knock Off, Rock Slide, Shadow Claw, Stone Edge, Throat Chop, Tera Blast, Aerial Ace

Niche Moves

Endure: Endure can sometimes be used in combination with Salac Berry to guarantee that Heracross survives an attack and receives a Speed boost. This is particularly useful for matchups where opportunities to use Trailblaze are limited and Heracross does not want to be locked into a move with Choice Scarf. It may also be combined with Endeavor to lower foes' HP to 1 before fainting or Reversal for an incredibly powerful Fighting-type attack.

Bullet Seed / Pin Missile / Rock Blast: Heracross possesses strong multi-hit moves that can be combined with Loaded Dice for strong attacks that are relatively more accurate than its standard options.

Pounce / Rock Tomb / Bulldoze: Rarely, Heracross can use a Speed-lowering move on foes that deal decent damage so it can threaten to outspeed and KO them the following turn.

Upper Hand: On Trailblaze setup variants, Heracross can sometimes use Upper Hand to outmaneuver revenge killers' priority moves.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: With a Choice Scarf, Heracross can be used as a decent revenge killer while also possessing sweep potential with Moxie.

Flame Orb: On Guts sets, Flame Orb is used to turn Heracross into a very powerful wallbreaker that is not locked into a move.

Niche Items

Damage-boosting items: If being burned isn't desirable or Heracross is using Moxie, it can instead use a damage-boosting item like Choice Band or Life Orb to increase its damage output.

Assault Vest: Heracross has workable Special Defense when paired with an Assault Vest, so it can be used to stomach some special attacks while still providing decent damage output with its high base Attack.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots can be used on more defensive Heracross variants to increase its longevity if entry hazards are a concern.

Salac Berry: Usually paired with Endure, Salac Berry can be used to give Heracross a Speed boost and let it snowball sweep with Moxie.

Custap Berry: Similar to Salac Berry, Custap Berry can be combined with Endure to let Heracross serve as an emergency check to an opposing foe.

Loaded Dice: When Heracross wants to use multi-hit moves, it can opt for Loaded Dice for consistency.

Focus Sash: Heracross can occasionally be used as a lead to deal significant damage early-game and maybe get up Spikes while doing so, and Focus Sash provides safety for these offensive lead sets.

Tera

Heracross is generally not drafted as a Tera Captain due to it not being a reliable wincon and it already possessing high immediate power, but it can still be effective with Tera. If Heracross is chosen as a Tera Captain, it can utilize Tera Normal to boost Facade on Guts sets to extremely high levels or Tera types such as Tera Ground and Dark to increase the power of its coverage moves. It also can use Tera Fighting effectively to increase its damage output from Close Combat, which is mostly useful on Choice Scarf sets.

Draft Strategy

Heracross fits on teams that are still looking for a physical wallbreaker and benefit from its resistance profile. It is capable of breaking almost every physical wall with the right set, but drafts should evaluate if they need power to the extent of Heracross or if something more flexible could be taken instead.

Slow Pivots: Heracross needs an opportunity to safely enter the field and activate its Flame Orb, and slow Pokemon with access to pivot moves such as Rotom-W, Galarian Slowking, and Mesprit can give Heracross this support.

Special Wallbreakers: Heracross fills the role of a physical wallbreaker for a team, and it likes being paired with a similarly strong special wallbreaker such as Chi-Yu, Gholdengo, or Thundurus-T to maintain offensive pressure both physically and specially.

Strong Entry Hazard Support: To enable Heracross's Choice Scarf cleaner sets, it appreciates entry hazards from Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Glimmora, and Sandy Shocks to weaken foes into range of its attacks.

Checks and Counters

Rocky Helmet: Heracross is prone to being worn down very quickly due to lacking recovery and often suffering from burn's chip damage. Rocky Helmet cuts into its longevity even more to the point where after it makes contact with one, Heracross is able to be revenge killed by pretty much everything.

Faster Pokemon: It's not difficult to outspeed Heracross, and since its bulk is only decent, fast offensive Pokemon such as Tornadus-T, Azelf, and Gouging Fire usually won't have much trouble in KOing it. Even Choice Scarf and Trailblaze variants are easily outsped by most opposing Choice Scarf users due to its mediocre base Speed.

Flying- and Fairy-types: Heracross's dual STAB combination is resisted by Flying- and Fairy-type Pokemon such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Zapdos, and Heracross is hit super effectively by both types, making them complicated to deal with, as they often force coverage and predictions.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description: Mega Heracross uses its gigantic Attack stat alongside Swords Dance to be a powerful wallbreaker, pressuring common physical walls like Skarmory and Mega Venusaur. Swords Dance boosts Mega Heracross's Attack to incredible heights and lets it OHKO a majority of the Pokemon in the tier, including walls like Skarmory and Hippowdon. Close Combat OHKOes threats like Tyranitar while 2HKOing bulkier Pokemon like Skarmory. Rock Blast threatens Flying-types such as Enamorus, Galarian Moltres, and Thundurus, as well as Fire-types like Iron Moth that could otherwise take Close Combat and force Mega Heracross out. Pin Missile threatens Slowbro and Mega Venusaur, while Substitute lets Mega Heracross avoid Will-O-Wisp from Mega Sableye, capitalize from the forced switches it generates, and ease prediction against Pokemon it forces out. Physical cleaners like Swords Dance Scizor appreciate Mega Heracross being able to threaten their switch-ins, such as Skarmory and Mega Venusaur, allowing them to sweep late-game. Mega Heracross is prone to being revenge killed by faster threats like Alakazam, Iron Moth, and Enamorus, so teammates that can deal with them such as Tyranitar and Celesteela, respectively, are appreciated. Fire-type partners like Victini and Iron Moth can threaten Buzzwole, which walls Mega Heracross; Poison-types like Amoonguss can threaten Fairy-types like Unaware Clefable, which also wall it.

movesets.name: All-out-Attacker
movesets.description: All-out attacker Mega Heracross functions as an incredible wallbreaker, being able to threaten common defensive staples such as Mega Venusaur, Celesteela and Slowbro with its fear-inducing Pin Missile and Close Combat off of its gargantuan base Attack stat. However, its poor typing and mediocre Speed cause it to be easily chipped down throughout the course of a game and forced out on many occasions. In addition, there are switch-ins to Mega Heracross, such as Buzzwole, that limit the damage it can do each time it switches in, as well as competition in the form of Buzzwole that can outlast it and deal more damage over the course of a game. Despite these flaws, though, Mega Heracross carves out a solid niche for itself in the NDUU metagame thanks to its raw power. Rock Blast nails the few Pokemon that resist both of Mega Heracross's STAB moves like Enamorus, Iron Moth, and Blacephalon. The final slot is interchangeable: Earthquake allows Mega Heracross to hit Aegislash, which otherwise would wall this set, while Trailblaze lets Mega Heracross patch up its middling Speed, outspeeding the likes of Alakazam and Mega Latias at +1, at the cost of being completely walled by Aegislash. Mega Heracross fits on balance teams that appreciate its ability to force tons of damage onto any foe and ease late-game cleanup. Hazard removers such as Excadrill and Defog Rotom-W allow Mega Heracross to find switch in opportunities without fearing Spikes set by Mew or Skarmory, while both help Mega Heracross in additional ways: Excadrill serves as a temporary stopgap to Fairy-types like Choice Scarf Enamorus and Clefable and scares Aegislash, while Rotom-W provides pivot opportunities for Mega Heracross to come in and wreak havoc. Celesteela is another great partner, as it is a far sturdier Fairy resistance alongside chip damage in the form of Leech Seed or cleaning potential with Autotomize; it also deals with Buzzwole, a major hurdle for Mega Heracross.
